children: It's Nvidia earnings day, and Bank of America clients have been dumping tech stocks.

Strategist Michael Hartnett said in the bank's latest fund manager survey that the net percentage of clients who were overweight tech fell by 25 percentage points this month — the biggest one-month drop since 2006.

Technology — formerly the favorite sector on Wall Street — has lately been weighed down by financing worries, while a sex-and-spy scandal has pummeled Nvidia shares this month and led to CEO Jensen Huang resigning.

Nvidia is down 24% in November, on pace for its biggest monthly decline since April 2022. That's helped drag down the S&P 500 tech sector by more than 8% in November alone, while the Nasdaq-100 index has shed 4.2%.
Sharp pullbacks and reallocations such as these have, in the past, signaled buying opportunities for investors. But, "we stay tactically risk-off," said Hartnett.

He noted that there is still not enough "fear" in the market to buy the dip. Hartnett said that cash allocation among clients remains at an "uber-low" 3.6%. Another 12% remain long the "Magnificent Seven" stocks (Amazon, Alphabet, Tesla, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia).

title: Investors lower tech stock exposure in biggest exit since 2006
